title: 30-17 Us. Decisive, For Once.
seoTitle: Commanders vs. Cardinals Prediction: Josh Johnson, Trey McBride, Sonny Styles and a 30-17 Call
summary: Commanders at Cardinals on Sunday: a 3-8 team that just fired its defensive coordinator, a 40-year-old quarterback on his 15th team, the one tight end who scares me, a defense that's finally fun, and a 30-17 pick for a win that doesn't come down to the last kick.
wireTaps: 30-17 us. For once, I want a win that isn't decided by a kicker. Too much to ask?
paragraphs: Hope everybody had a great Thanksgiving. I hope you ate too much and someone at the table said something about the Cowboys that made you smile. Mine was the Eagles beating Dallas. I cheered harder for the Eagles on Thursday than I have in a very long time, and it hurt my heart, and I was still happy. That's where we are.

Here's the thing. This is the best I've felt all season. Two wins in a row, the first back-to-back of the year, and the defense is actually fun to watch. Which is exactly the scary part. Every time I've felt this good about this team, something has happened. I'm aware. I'm doing it anyway.

So my pick is Commanders 30, Cardinals 17. We finally win a game decisively. No walk-off field goal. No 46-second drill. No last-play heroics. I would like, just once, to watch the fourth quarter with my heart rate under 140.

And for once I'm the reasonable one. Four of you have already called your shot and every single one of you has us winning. 28-21, 31-17, 35-10, and one absolute maniac with 33-9. You people went from BOLD to bloodthirsty in one week and I love it.
Links up top, like always: [who's reffing Sunday](whos-reffing.html), and [Call Your Shot](leaderboard.html), where you can get your pick in before the 4:25 kickoff.
## The Cardinals Are a Mess

I want to be careful here, because Jayden spent part of his press conference this week talking about how the Cardinals are a good team that could punch us in the mouth. That's very kind of him. Jayden is a nice young man and he was raised right. I was not, so I'll say it: the Cardinals are a mess.

They're 3-8. They've lost three straight. Their defense has given up 30 or more points in eight of eleven games, and the morning after a 34-7 loss in Kansas City they fired their defensive coordinator. The team podcast counted four different quarterbacks in four weeks. Their rookie, Carson Beck, is out with back spasms, so on Sunday it's Josh Johnson.

Josh Johnson is 40 years old. He's been on 14 NFL teams before this one, and one of them was us. He is the journeyman's journeyman. I mean that with real respect, because you don't stick around that long without knowing football, and Dan Quinn spent his Friday presser praising how few looks Josh Johnson hasn't seen. He can run an offense. That's about where the bar is, though. Last week he went 18-of-31 for 155 yards in that Kansas City game. Our defense just held Joe Burrow's offense to 20 points.

So I asked myself, honestly: outside of Trey McBride, what does Arizona really have? They do have some names. Budda Baker is still back there and Josh Sweat can still rush the passer. But the defense is the one that just got its coordinator fired, and the offense is a 40-year-old guy throwing to a tight end. This is a team we should beat. Not squeak by. Beat.
## The One That Scares Me: Trey McBride

McBride is second in the NFL in targets and catches. He's a tight end, and we cannot cover a tight end. Mike Gesicki had five catches for 77 yards on us Monday night, most of them with somebody draped on him. Daronte Jones said this week that because McBride lines up close to the line, it's on the linebackers and safeties to read their keys and track him at the same time. That sounds hard. It sounds like the kind of thing that ends with a 45-yard catch over the middle while I yell at my TV.
So yes, I'm budgeting for one stupid deep ball to McBride on Sunday. Maybe two. I've accepted it. I've made peace with it in advance, which might be the most mature thing I've done all year.
## Dan Quinn's Guys Would Run Through Walls

Dan Quinn has his flaws as a coach. We've all seen them. We've all yelled about them in a group chat at 11 PM. But if there's one thing Dan Quinn can do, it's get people to play for him. Guys would run through a lot of walls for that man. The team message this week was simple: "can you do it again?" Then he told them to close the airplane doors and get ready for a dogfight in the desert. I'm not a football player and I wanted to run through a wall after reading that.

This is also the kind of game where a motivated team should just take care of business. Trap game? Sure, on paper. A 3-8 team at home, a long flight, a short week after a huge Monday night. But Jayden summed up the mood in the building pretty perfectly: "winning cures everything." I'll take it.
## The D Is Fun Now

I can't believe I'm writing that heading, but it's true. Jason, in the group chat, the morning after the Bengals game: "I [very strong adverb] LOVE Sonny Styles. He's the most fun defender to watch that we've had since I can remember." I told him Styles reminds me of a bigger London Fletcher, and I stand by it. Even when he doesn't get the sack, he blows up running backs in pass protection, and that running back is going to feel it the next day. The team podcast calls him the SS Impala. I call him my favorite player right now.

Jason also loves that Daronte Jones will just send dudes. Jones's version is a little more polished. He said the goal is to "dictate the terms and try to be aggressive." Same thing. If we get pressure on Josh Johnson the way we got it on Burrow, and we should, I like our chances a lot.

The one thing this defense can't do yet is catch. We dropped somewhere between four interceptions (Chris's count) and eight (mine, and I'm sticking with it) against the Bengals. Chris had the right response at 11:15 PM Monday night: "This week at practice the defense works on catching." We're down Mike Sainristil and Amik Robertson again, so it's Rasul Douglas and Fabian Moreau back there, and Daronte Jones liked what he saw from both of them. Just hang onto one, guys. One.
## The Group Chat Was Right About the Snaps

On Monday night, Jason spent a good part of the game yelling about Lucas Patrick's shotgun snaps. "These snaps are soooooo slow." "OMG THESE SNAPS." Chris, completely deadpan: "He's a center. Why does snapping matter?" Then, on Tuesday, Dan Quinn walked to the podium and said the shotgun snaps were inconsistent in location and speed. On Thursday, David Blough called it "certainly something to improve on." Jason, you were right. Enjoy it. It doesn't happen often.
## Aiyuk, Briefly

Brandon Aiyuk is on the practice squad and won't play Sunday. He and Jayden go back to Arizona State, where Aiyuk looked out for an 18-year-old Jayden, and whatever happened over the summer, the two of them settled it like grown men. Jayden said Aiyuk is like a brother to him and said getting the chemistry back would be "like riding the bike again." Quinn said his first impression was a good one. I'm trying to be patient. I've already penciled him in for the playoff game we're definitely going to be in.
## A Few More Things

On the team podcast, Santana Moss ordered vanilla ice cream for Antonio Williams, because it'll be hot in Arizona. Treylon Burks got crowned the flag guy for how much pass interference he draws, with the plea "Feed him the ball more please. It's Thanksgiving." Seconded. David Blough said Jayden's two big throws on the final drive Monday reminded him of Teddy Bridgewater. And Dan Quinn still owes everyone an answer on whether Stefon Diggs tackled Antonio Williams on purpose on the last play. He said he'd follow up. I'm following up.
Ref Watch, quickly: Land Clark has the game, and his crews are among the quietest in the league. If we get flagged a bunch Sunday, that one's on us.
## The Pick

Jason said before the Bengals game that the next three, Arizona, Tennessee and Houston, are really the season, and that we pretty much need all three. I think he's right. And you have to start with the one you're supposed to win.

So here's what I see. We get pressure early. Josh Johnson does Josh Johnson things, some good, mostly not. McBride gets his deep ball and I scream. Jayden starts fast for once, Bill Croskey-Merritt runs downhill, and by the fourth quarter I'm relaxed. Relaxed! On a Sunday! Imagine.
Commanders 30, Cardinals 17.
Sunday, 4:25 on FOX. Hail.
